sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGL compatibility, Three.js TSL, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Web Audio API, Gamepad API, WebRTC, BroadcastChannel, AI Hub session client
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded / ink illustration; ivory ice, navy ink, golden Foxes and cyan Freeze
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and native keyframe tracks; skating and stick swings, procedural stun and goal particles
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written rink-organ / chiptune music, synthesized effects and Animalese / Simlish-style gibberish announcer; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: Two-player AI Hub shared-world host authority; standalone WebRTC invite / answer; same-origin browser-tab rooms via BroadcastChannel. Direct WebRTC has STUN but no TURN relay.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium WebGPU and WebGL compatibility, scripted physics and match / skills playthroughs, two-page multiplayer, emulated standard gamepad and touch, offline synthesized audio analysis. Physical controller, real touchscreen, real iOS and cross-NAT network behavior: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet research. Native model knowledge for source and design. Retrieved the user-specified AI Hub integration code and exact runtime dependencies.

testingFeedback: Testing and implementation review caught 12 distinct issues: a Rapier API mismatch, six multiplayer/lifecycle bugs, three input edge cases, opponent skills progression, and AI Wild Shot behavior. All were fixed and the final suite passed.
2 critical issues: a Rapier descriptor method mismatch prevented startup; multiplayer throttling could discard guest action commands. Both were fixed.
The real Rapier scripted match and skills playthroughs, which exercised scoring, period transitions, sudden death and all five skills steps.

The initial headless WebGPU screenshot was blank; runtime state assertions and WebGL compatibility screenshots were more useful. The initial title screenshot test also outlasted the attract timer, so the test now freezes idle only during capture.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL made banded cel lighting and ink-shell characters straightforward, and native AnimationMixer clips fit procedural players.
Guessed one Rapier descriptor method name incorrectly; runtime testing exposed it. Browser input and multiplayer throttling also required explicit integration checks.
The full hockey simulation: puck possession, skater AI, keepers, passes, charged shots, checking, periods and host-authoritative replication.
Coordinating fixed-step Rapier physics, puck possession and network snapshots with browser rendering and input.
A more direct built-in path for headless WebGPU image readback and screenshot testing.
promptFeedback: The clear single-file deliverable, controller-first direction and required attract mode made the intended experience concrete.
No plan file was supplied. The no-research instruction and required online integration URL were interpreted as allowing retrieval of integration code without source research.
Finishing gameplay, three input families, real multiplayer, procedural art/audio and verification together as one polished vertical slice.
Provide a pinned downloadable AI Hub integration package and clarify whether standalone online play should include a hosted relay.

aiHub.name: Ice Hockey Puck Wild
aiHub.description: A cel-shaded arcade hockey night with slippery skating, sharp passes, big checks, and wild slapshots. Play three quick periods against the Freeze, learn in Skills Club, or face a friend locally or online.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick skate; mouse / right stick aim; hold Space / Square shoot; E / Cross pass; F / Circle check; Q / L1 switch; Shift / R1 boost; Esc / Options pause.
